messages.content: Write a nomination for an internal engineering award, for a team that improved the deployment process. Around 200 words.

output:
Here's a draft. I left bracketed spots for the details only you have — swap in real numbers and it'll land harder.

---

**Nomination: [Team name] — Engineering Excellence Award**

A year ago, shipping to production meant a Wednesday-night window, a 40-step checklist nobody trusted, and two people on standby in case the rollback went sideways. Releases took four hours. Half of them slipped.

[Team] rebuilt it. They replaced the hand-run checklist with a pipeline that builds, tests, and promotes on merge, added automated canary analysis so a bad release rolls itself back in under [90 seconds], and cut deploy time from [4 hours to 11 minutes]. Deploy frequency went from [weekly to ~30 times a week]. Change-failure rate dropped by [X%].

What I want to call out is how they did it. No big-bang rewrite, no six-month freeze. They migrated one service at a time, kept the old path working alongside the new one, and sat with each team through their first few deploys until it stuck. [Name] wrote the migration guide that made it self-serve for everyone else.

The result is quieter on-call, faster fixes, and engineers who ship without asking permission. That's infrastructure work at its best — the kind you only notice once it's gone.

---

Roughly 200 words. Want a shorter version, or one aimed at a non-engineering award committee?
